findings.finding: The ADR-045 pin's docstring asserted an invariant the package already violates: dev_server/state.py does a module-scope `from lib.atomic_write import ...` reached via __init__.py, so `import dev_server` ALWAYS binds sys.modules['lib']. The test pinned a far narrower fact than it claimed.
AC5 was pinned by nothing. Ledger row 7 claimed a wrong _SCRIPTS_DIR would break the deferred import; it would not, because state.py already inserts shared/scripts into sys.path at import.
Subprocess probe embedded a path via r'{}'.format(); an apostrophe or backslash escape in the repo path would be a child SyntaxError.
subprocess.run(text=True) without encoding decodes with the host locale codec (cp1252 on the F0 host); a non-ASCII byte in a child traceback would raise UnicodeDecodeError in the parent.
Two adjacent rationale blocks overlapped, and the pre-existing banner repeated the sys.modules['lib'] claim shown false by finding 1.
Docstring claim 'nothing here reads os.name' is not literally true of the function - the tail call reaches cmd_resolver, which reads os.name by design.
The same shared/scripts constant is derived two ways in one package (os.path here, pathlib in state.py), both inserting into sys.path.

Claim under doubt: the shipped comment's account of how pathlib fails under a faked os.name — 'Constructing Path(x) is safe, only derivations raise' holds on 3.12 but is FALSE on 3.11, where Path.__new__ checks _flavour.is_supported so construction itself raises. Every CI workflow pins 3.11 via `uv python install 3.11`, while uv run locally picks 3.12+ - so the claim was measured on an interpreter the gate never uses. No behavioural break, because the fix removes pathlib from the lazy body outright; the damage is the invitation to write a bare Path() back in and ship a 3.11-only failure that is green locally and red on ubuntu-latest, which is the exact failure shape this iterate exists to remove.
